title: Project Director
purpose: Provide ultimate project delivery leadership and accountability (scope, schedule, budget, client relationship), while ensuring BIM governance is respected and resourced. The senior decision-maker who resolves cross-functional conflicts and authorizes material project changes, including those affecting information delivery.
authority_statements: Approve project-wide delivery strategy, resourcing, and major milestone commitments
Authorize scope, schedule, and budget changes and their tradeoffs
Direct escalation resolution when discipline teams or governance leads cannot reach alignment
Approve contractual commitments and major client-facing decisions (including BIM-related commitments when they impact contract delivery)
May approve BEP adoption as a project instrument after governance review
May approve project resourcing required to meet information delivery obligations
May approve changes to milestone dates that impact information delivery submissions
May approve acceptance of project-level deviation requests with executive sign-off requirements
May reject unfunded or unrealistic delivery expectations
May reject requests to bypass governance processes (skipping validation, bypassing deliverable acceptance gates)
May reject tool/process changes introduced mid-project without impact assessment and governance alignment
May not override constitutional constraints on permitted use, authority boundaries, and governed information integrity
May not override defined acceptance/validation requirements once contractually committed
May not override BIM governance decisions within delegated authority of BIM Manager unless escalated through defined path
responsibilities: Own the overall project delivery outcome and ensure cross-discipline alignment to achieve it
Ensure BIM governance is resourced and empowered (people, time, coordination cadence) to meet information delivery requirements
Ensure the project has an approved project delivery plan that includes information delivery responsibilities and acceptance gates
Resolve escalations when delivery conflicts arise between design intent, schedule/budget realities, and governance requirements
Ensure contractual BIM commitments are understood at leadership level and are consistent with TIVERIT Standards and permitted use boundaries
Sponsor and protect governance discipline (standards adherence, validation, controlled deviations) as a project leadership duty
Ensure client communication is aligned and truthful regarding deliverable readiness, limitations, and permitted use
accountabilities: Highest level of leadership accountable for BIM deliverables as part of overall project success
Ultimate accountability for scope, schedule, budget, and client confidence
Ensuring the project can meet its information delivery obligations without overpromising or bypassing governance
approvals: Overall project delivery and major milestones
Acceptance of BIM deliverables as part of project scope
Risk acceptance where BIM constraints impact scope/schedule
Project BEP adoption at project level
Project-level Deviation / Exception Records at executive level
inputs: Project Delivery Strategy and Contract Documents
Project BEP and MIDP/TIDP proposals from Project BIM Manager
Escalation requests from Project Manager and Project BIM Manager
outputs: Executive client commitments and change approvals
Escalation outcomes and final arbitration decisions
Final sign-off on BIM-related project deliverables (as part of overall handover)
